author: Timur Doumler

evidence.note: R1 proposed applying Contracts (P2900R9) semantics to undefined behaviour; the R8 revision history shows the direction persisted while preprocessor UB and non-UB items were removed and the paper was retargeted to C++29.
evidence.title: P3100R1: Undefined and erroneous behaviour is a contract violation
evidence.what_changed: Between R1 and R8 Doumler kept the core direction (apply Contracts semantics to UB via implicit contract assertions, replacing UB with erroneous behaviour) but conceded or adjusted scope repeatedly: R2 was a complete rewrite to target the core-language UB white paper (P3656R1); R3 removed preprocessor UB after P2843R3 was adopted into C++26; R4 dropped UB-list items that should not be specified as UB and have Core issues, added a noexcept interaction discussion, and changed the title to reflect the wider scope; R6 added full wording targeting C++29 after EWG requested it.

evidence.note: Herb Sutter reports that at the 2026 Brno meeting EWG approved line-by-line telecon review of P3100 "A framework for systematically addressing undefined behaviour in the C++ Standard" by Timur Doumler and Joshua Berne, targeting inclusion in C++29, and describes systematically addressing C++ UB as enormously important and historic.

evidence.title: P3229R1: Making erroneous behaviour compatible with Contracts

position: Timur Doumler has consistently and publicly argued, from P3100's R0 formulation of "undefined and erroneous behaviour are contract violations" through R8, that core-language undefined behaviour in C++ should be systematically addressed rather than treated case-by-case. His documented program is to enumerate all core-language UB (paired with the adopted P3596 UB/IFNDR annexes), insert runtime checks via implicit contract assertions built on C++26 Contracts (P2900), and replace UB with erroneous but well-defined behaviour wherever possible, as detailed in his Sofia 2025 EWG presentation P3754R0. Across revisions he conceded scope adjustments — removing preprocessor UB after P2843R3, dropping cases better handled as Core issues, and adopting the white-paper/holistic framing targeting C++29 — but never gave up the runtime-check-plus-erroneous-behaviour core. Committee records he accepted (SG21 Wrocław, EWG Sofia/Hagenberg, SG23 Kona, EWG Croydon, EWG Brno line-by-line review) all moved the same direction, and his companion papers P3229 and P3874 tie this framework to Contracts and to the C++ memory-safety effort.
recommendation: The paper proposes a holistic strategy for systematically detecting, mitigating, and eliminating core language undefined behaviour in the C++ Standard. It recommends introducing runtime checks via implicit contract assertions and replacing undefined behaviour with erroneous but well-defined behaviour wherever possible, and provides proposed wording targeting C++29.
title: A framework for systematically addressing undefined behaviour in the C++ Standard
